nodes.label: DiceManager (DiceBoxState machine)
nodes.rationale: Knows nothing about mana or combat; gravity overridden only while Rolling; never hides the overlay

nodes.label: Combat Log Panel
nodes.rationale: Footer text log records 'Combat begins: Drowned Wretch, Vault Rat.' and 'Turn 1: rolled B R R R B B. Pool: Red 3, Blue 3, Yellow 0.' as a readable history of rolls and pool.

nodes.label: Combat Screen Layout (enemies top, mana+dice middle, heroes bottom, log footer)
nodes.norm_label: combat screen layout (enemies top, mana+dice middle, heroes bottom, log footer)
nodes.rationale: Three-band layout keeps threats (enemy intents) above, shared resources (mana pool + rolled dice chips) in the centre, and the party's spend options (ability buttons per hero) below, so the player reads threat -> resources -> actions top to bottom. Placeholder panels with TMP text per prototype fidelity rules.

nodes.label: Enemy Cards with Telegraphed Intents
nodes.rationale: Each enemy card (Drowned Wretch 10/10 'Next: Attack 5', Vault Rat 8/8 'Next: Attack 3') shows a red health bar and the next intent with a sword icon, telegraphing damage so the player can plan shields/taunt.

nodes.label: Hero Cards with Ability Buttons
nodes.rationale: Each hero card is tinted in the hero's colour domain with a green health bar and three ability buttons labelled with cost (1/2/3 of the hero colour) and an icon.

nodes.label: Mana Pool Display (Red 3, Blue 3, Yellow 0, Turn 1)
nodes.norm_label: mana pool display (red 3, blue 3, yellow 0, turn 1)
nodes.rationale: Shared party colour mana pool, one mana per settled resource die; shown with the turn counter so carried-over mana is visible across turns.

nodes.label: Resource Dice Chips (6 dice: B R R R B B)
nodes.norm_label: resource dice chips (6 dice: b r r r b b)
nodes.rationale: One chip per rolled die shows pips plus a colour letter on a colour-tinted tile (pips 1-2 Red, 3-4 Blue, 5-6 Yellow), so die-targeted abilities (Reroll, Recolour) have a visible target.

nodes.rationale: Header hint explains the resource-dice rule: each die adds one mana of its colour, mana carries between turns. The phrase 'as often as it lasts' implies unlimited casts, which may predate the one-ability-per-hero-per-turn default; the screenshot may be stale relative to that rule.

nodes.label: Telegraphed Enemy Intent Display
nodes.rationale: Each enemy card shows a sword icon and its next action ('Next: Attack N') so the player can plan before spending mana.

nodes.rationale: Instructions sit on the overlay itself because everything under the dice overlay is covered while it is open; the banner reads 'Turn 1: drag across the box to throw the party's 6 resource dice (1-2 Red, 3-4 Blue, 5-6 Yellow)'. nodes.label: DiceManager pooled-count and m_isIdle bugs

nodes.label: One ScriptableObject/MonoBehaviour per file
nodes.rationale: Unity binds assets to scripts by file name; a class in another file loads with m_Script fileID 0 (null)

nodes.label: PhysX decides the face-up result
nodes.rationale: The player's drag-throw stays; settled face becomes a logical RollResult that modifiers change and the die re-orients to

nodes.label: Fork Edge Labels (threshold + unlock chance)
nodes.rationale: Each fork edge shows its threshold ('any', '7+', '9+', '12+', '14+') and, once dice are committed, the chance of unlocking: any 100%, 7+ 17%, 12+ 0% for Low Road + Steady. Chances are non-exclusive so they do not sum to 1.

nodes.label: UI Issue: Edge Label Overlaps Antechamber Card
nodes.norm_label: ui issue: edge label overlaps antechamber card
nodes.rationale: The '11+' threshold label renders on top of the Antechamber card text, and The Warden's type reads 'E ite'; edge labels are placed at edge midpoints without collision avoidance.

nodes.label: Map Screen Act Graph (left-to-right columns)
nodes.rationale: Nodes laid out in columns by longest path from Start (Vault Gate) to Boss (The Vault Heart), rows within a column; each card shows type icon, name and node type; current node highlighted in accent gold.

nodes.label: Node Detail Panel (Vault Gate, Start)
nodes.rationale: Below the graph: node name, type, description ('The way in. Three doors; the higher you roll, the more of them open.'), instruction 'roll 1-3 dice', dice toggles, odds disclaimer and a full-width Roll button.

nodes.label: Map Header: Party HP, Resource Dice, Traversal Dice
nodes.norm_label: map header: party hp, resource dice, traversal dice
nodes.rationale: Summary line: Knight 30/30, Arcanist 20/20, Trickster 24/24 | 6 resource dice | traversal dice Low Road, Steady, High Road.

nodes.label: Prototype Act Nodes (Vault Gate to The Vault Heart)
nodes.norm_label: prototype act nodes (vault gate to the vault heart)
nodes.rationale: 11 nodes visible: Vault Gate (Start); Forgotten Cache (Treasure), Drowned Hall (Combat), The Warden (Elite); Dry Alcove (Rest); Flooded Stair (Combat), Chained Golem (Elite), Sealed Reliquary (Treasure); Last Lantern (Rest); Antechamber (Combat); The Vault Heart (Boss). Three forks: Vault Gate, Dry Alcove (any/9+/14+), and an 11+ fork near Antechamber.

nodes.label: Traversal Dice Commit Toggles
nodes.rationale: Each traversal die shows its pip faces: Low Road [1 1 2 2 3 3], Steady [3 3 3 4 4 4], High Road [4 4 5 5 6 6]. Committed dice are gold (Low Road and Steady here); button reads 'Roll 2 dice'. Note: 'Nominal odds for fair dice; the throw decides' because PhysX decides the face.

nodes.label: Roll-to-Unlock-then-Choose Fork Rule
nodes.rationale: On-screen hint: 'A fork: commit dice and roll. The total unlocks every path at or below it; you choose.' An always-open 'any' path guarantees a roll can never strand the party.

nodes.label: Combat Log Panel
nodes.rationale: Bottom text log records combat start and each turn's rolled colours and resulting pool ("Turn 1: rolled B R R R B B. Pool: Red 3, Blue 3, Yellow 0.").

nodes.label: Resource Die Chips (pips + colour letter)
nodes.rationale: One chip per settled resource die (six here: B R R R B B), coloured by mana colour with pip face and a colour letter, so the pool's origin is visible and die-targeted abilities (Reroll, Recolour) have something to click.

nodes.label: Enemy Cards (Drowned Wretch 10/10, Vault Rat 8/8)
nodes.rationale: Top row of full-width enemy cards with red health bars; during targeting the intent body is replaced by a 'Click to target' prompt. A regular Combat node shows two regular enemies.

nodes.label: Enemy Targeting Mode (Strike: click an enemy)
nodes.norm_label: enemy targeting mode (strike: click an enemy)
nodes.rationale: Single-target abilities enter a targeting mode: the header prompt names the ability, enemy cards are highlighted gold with 'Click to target', and a Cancel button backs out without spending mana or the hero's action.

nodes.label: Hero Cards with Ability Buttons (Knight, Arcanist, Trickster)
nodes.norm_label: hero cards with ability buttons (knight, arcanist, trickster)
nodes.rationale: Bottom row, one card per hero tinted in the hero's colour domain, green HP bar (30/30, 20/20, 24/24) and three icon-labelled ability buttons with cost (1/2/3 of the hero colour).

nodes.norm_label: colour domains (red damage/block, blue statuses, yellow dice modification)
nodes.rationale: Hero card tints and ability icons map each hero to one mana colour, making which rolled dice pay for which hero readable at a glance.

nodes.label: Opposite faces sum to 7
nodes.rationale: Historically correct d6 numbering; lets Flip be computed as 7 - face

nodes.label: Fork threshold rule (roll to unlock, then choose)
nodes.norm_label: fork threshold rule (roll to unlock, then choose)
nodes.rationale: A roll unlocks every path at or below its total; ForkValidator guarantees a path at the lowest total so a roll never strands the party

nodes.label: Fork bracket rule (full coverage, no gaps)
nodes.norm_label: fork bracket rule (full coverage, no gaps)
nodes.rationale: The player never fails a roll; superseded by threshold unlock-then-choose forks

nodes.label: Screenshot: Traversal Pick screen
nodes.description: 1920x1080 capture of the Traversal Pick phase: gold title 'Choose your traversal dice', explainer subtitle, 'Pick 3 more. Click a chosen die to put it back.' prompt, four equal-width dark placeholder cards in a row (one per traversal die, listing faces, mean and a one-line playstyle), and a full-width gold 'Enter the dungeon' button at the bottom. Nothing selected yet; cards are mostly empty space below the text.

nodes.label: Enter the dungeon button
nodes.rationale: Confirms the traversal selection and enters the act (ConfirmTraversalDice); shown dimmed while fewer than three dice are chosen.

nodes.label: Fork roll explainer text
nodes.rationale: Subtitle reads 'At every fork you commit dice and roll; the total picks the path. Different faces, different odds.' This wording predates the 2026-10-20 threshold rule (total unlocks paths, player chooses), so the screenshot copy may be stale.

nodes.label: High Road die (4 4 5 5 6 6, mean 5.0)
nodes.rationale: Chases high totals (unlocks higher-threshold Elite/Treasure/Boss paths).

nodes.label: Low Road die (1 1 2 2 3 3, mean 2.0)
nodes.rationale: Chases low totals.

nodes.label: Steady die (3 3 3 4 4 4, mean 3.5)
nodes.rationale: Hits the middle; low variance.

nodes.label: Traversal Pick screen layout
nodes.rationale: Code-built uGUI placeholder layout: header + instructions column, a flexible row of four die cards, fixed-height confirm button. Each card exposes faces and mean so the player can reason about fork odds before committing.

nodes.label: Wild die (1 1 1 6 6 6, mean 3.5)
nodes.rationale: All or nothing; same mean as Steady but maximum variance.

nodes.label: Pick 3 distinct of 4 starting traversal dice
nodes.norm_label: pick 3 distinct of 4 starting traversal dice
nodes.rationale: Prompt 'Pick 3 more. Click a chosen die to put it back.' shows the selection is toggleable and requires three dice before entering the dungeon.
